old: As a customer, I want to register for a local or tourist account and maintain my profile and addresses so that I can place an order using my customer details.
As a customer, I want to browse active hubs, brands and available items so that I can choose what and where to order.
As a customer, I want to review the complete quote, voucher and payment choice before confirming so that I can make an informed order decision.
As a user, I want to log in and log out with role-appropriate access so that each task is performed by an authorised account.
As an administrator, I want to create, read, update and archive hubs and maintain capacity so that current hub operations are represented.
As a customer, I want a full hub to refuse the order and present eligible quieter hubs so that I can choose another option before confirming.
As kitchen staff, I want to confirm or reject an incoming order, or offer a valid replacement, so that I can handle an order against current stock.
As a customer, I want to track my order, view its receipt and answer an open replacement offer so that I can see and decide the order outcome.
As kitchen staff, I want to start preparation and mark an order READY so that a shipper can take a prepared order.
As kitchen staff, I want to change availability for items at my hub so that new orders use the current listing.
As a shipper, I want to take a ready order and record delivery, exact COD cash or a failed outcome so that fulfilment is traceable per order.
As an administrator, I want to maintain brands, menu items and hub listings so that customers see the catalogue used by the kitchens.
As an administrator, I want to create, update and archive vouchers so that eligible customers can use the configured discount rules.
As a customer, I want to cancel my own order while it is PLACED or CONFIRMED so that an early cancellation follows the defined payment rules.
As an administrator, I want to create accounts and deactivate or reactivate them so that access can be maintained.
As an administrator, I want to archive closed orders and read their history so that operational lists stay current while authorised history remains available.
As a manager, I want reports for sales, hub workload and delivery performance so that I can compare operations using shared definitions.
As a customer, I want rejection, cancellation, replacement and delivery-failure outcomes to show the correct payment state and amount owed so that I know what remains due.
As a reviewer, I want postcondition, boundary, role and concurrency tests for each main use case so that release claims have recorded evidence.

Capacity cannot be set below one. It may be lowered below current load, after which the hub refuses new orders until load drops. Archive succeeds only when every order is DELIVERED, DELIVERY_FAILED, REJECTED, or CANCELLED; otherwise it is refused.

Case p.2 sales report feature; Plan §3.4 BR-20/Q5, BR-21/Q5, BR-24/Q5; A-07/Q5

Stored timestamps are UTC. The inclusive Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh calendar-date inputs define [start 00:00, end+1 00:00), converted to UTC; a delivery is included by finish time, never order placement time. The system shall report delivery waiting time, successful ride time, and the delivery failure rate for a Vietnam-calendar date range.
Case p.2 delivery-performance report feature; Plan §3.4 BR-20/Q5 and BR-23/Q5; A-07/Q5

Only deliveries finished within the same half-open Vietnam-day interval defined in FR-24 are selected. Case p.1 hub-staff feature and p.2 private contact data; Plan §2.1 UC-05; §3.2 BR-26; §4.1 kitchen transitions

The system shall allow a kitchen replacement offer only for an unavailable line on an own-hub PLACED order and only when its proposed target meets the locked eligibility rules.
Case p.1 unavailable-item substitution problem; Plan §3.3 items 1–3; §3.2 BR-26; §4.4 ReplacementOffer; A-06

The source dish must currently be sold out, unlisted, or archived at that hub. The offer proposes replacement of the whole line at unchanged quantity; it changes no order line before customer acceptance. The target is ACTIVE, listed, AVAILABLE, different from the source, not already on the order, and no more expensive than the source snapshot. Cross-brand targets are allowed. At most one offer is OFFERED per order at a time; a later offer may follow a resolved one while the order stays PLACED.
The system shall preserve resolved replacement offers as history and show the customer the complete offered change before an answer is submitted.
Case p.1 substitution problem and full-price consent feature; Plan §3.3 items 2 and 4; §2.2 SUC-03; A-06

The customer sees original and new names and prices, quantity, proposed new total, and ONLINE refund owed before answering. The customer can still read resolved offer history, and at most one offer is open at a time.
The system shall block kitchen confirmation and preparation while an order has an open replacement offer.
Case p.1 substitution problem and preparation feature; Plan §3.3 item 4; §4.1 confirmOrder/startPreparing; A-06
While an offer is OFFERED, confirm and start-preparing requests leave both order and offer unchanged. After the offer resolves, the order may continue only if its state permits.
The system shall revalidate ownership, order state, the exact open offer, and target availability when a customer accepts a replacement.
Case p.1 substitution problem and full-price consent feature; Plan §3.3 item 5; §4.1 acceptReplacement; A-06

Acceptance is applied in one transaction only for the owning customer, a PLACED order, the exact OFFERED offer, and a target still listed, available, and not archived. If the target is invalid, the offer becomes WITHDRAWN with a reason, the order remains unchanged, and the customer sees a message. A valid acceptance uses the offered price even if catalogue price later changed.
The system shall recalculate replacement totals using the service-recovery concession and keep COD payable and ONLINE refund owed distinct.
Case p.1 substitution, price, and online-payment needs; Plan §3.3 items 6–7 and oracle example; §3.1 BR-09; A-06/A-16

On acceptance, D_new = min(D_old, S_new); voucher terms are not re-evaluated and F and Q do not change. COD is payable at new T. The system shall record a customer’s replacement decline as rejection and make stale or repeated answers harmless.
Case p.1 substitution problem and p.2 lifecycle fixed fact; Plan §3.3 items 8–10; §3.2 BR-17; §4.1 declineReplacement; L3; A-06/A-09/L3

The system shall let own-hub kitchen staff start preparing a CONFIRMED order and mark a PREPARING order READY.
Case p.1 preparation and ready features; Plan §2.2 SUC-05; §4.1/§4.2
Only a CONFIRMED own-hub order can become PREPARING. Only a PREPARING own-hub order can become READY; that transition records ready time and creates one AWAITING_PICKUP delivery.
The system shall let kitchen staff set availability for a listing at their own hub.
Case p.1 availability feature; Plan §2.2 SUC-06; §4.4 listing states; §3.2 BR-26

An authorized staff member can switch an own-hub listing between AVAILABLE and SOLD_OUT. A cross-hub update is rejected, and SOLD_OUT is represented on the listing rather than as a global menu-item state.
The system shall let an admin create, read, update, and archive brands and menu items while preserving existing order snapshots.
Case p.2 catalogue administration feature; Plan §2.1 UC-06; §3.2 BR-19; §2.4 Brand/MenuItem
Admin can complete the listed create/read/update/archive operations. Price or name changes leave existing order lines unchanged. An archived brand or item cannot be newly listed or ordered.
The system shall let an admin create, read, update, and unlist hub-menu listings.
Case p.2 menu administration feature; Plan §2.4 HubMenuItem; §2.4 CRUD union; §4.4 listing states
Admin can create and view a listing, update its hub-specific availability, and unlist it. Unlisting removes the operational association while saved order-line snapshots remain readable.
The system shall let an admin create, read, update, and archive vouchers.
Case p.2 voucher administration feature; Plan §2.2 SUC-07; §3.1 BR-08/A-16
Admin can complete each operation. An archived voucher is excluded from checkout; an active voucher is applied only under FR-09 conditions.
The system shall let an admin create, read, update, deactivate, and reactivate user accounts subject to delivery and session guards.
Case p.2 account administration feature; Plan §2.2 SUC-08; §3.2 BR-25; §4.4 UserAccount

Admin can complete the listed operations. Deactivation blocks the account on its next request. A shipper holding a PICKED_UP delivery cannot be deactivated; after the delivery is no longer PICKED_UP, the guard is re-evaluated.
The system shall let an admin archive only closed orders and let authorized users read archived history.
Requirements p.2 §2.1 persistent-class CRUD; Case p.2 management reports; Plan §2.2 SUC-09; §2.4 Order; §3.4 BR-24/Q5; §5.3 schema contract; A-07/Q5

Only DELIVERED, DELIVERY_FAILED, REJECTED, or CANCELLED orders can be archived. Archived orders disappear from operational lists but remain available in authorized history, receipts, reports, and refund-obligation views; the archive operation does not physically delete the order or its related rows.

Plan D-5; §5.2 persistent local disk; §5.3 schema

Create an order, recreate the application container, then reboot the demo VM and retrieve the same authorized order ID with identical S/D/F/Q/T and payment state. This is a deployment target until measured in P6.
The system shall respond to each designated key page in under one second on the demo VM.
Phase 1 checklist P1-17; Plan D-5 deployment target

For customer browse, quote, order/receipt, kitchen queue, shipper READY board, admin catalogue, and manager report pages, run 20 warm requests per page on the demo VM; each response target is below 1,000 ms. This target is unmeasured and must be labelled as such until P6 evidence exists.
The system shall restrict passport disclosure to the owning customer and authorized admin views and keep it off kitchen and shipper pages and logs.

Use a synthetic Tourist record with a unique passport sentinel, fetch every kitchen and shipper page plus unauthorized customer and manager requests, and inspect captured application logs; the sentinel must occur zero times. Only the owning customer and authorized admin views may show it. Measurement: exact string scan; no result recorded in P1.
The system shall reject state-changing browser requests without a valid CSRF token.
Plan §5.1 presentation forms and §5.4 CSRF rule

For every state-changing POST operation, a missing or invalid token is rejected and makes zero persistent changes; a valid token proceeds subject to business rules. Measurement: enumerate POST routes, compare relevant row contents and counts, and require total_changes delta zero for rejected requests. CSRF tokens and checkout idempotency tokens are independently checked; no result recorded in P1.
The system shall keep production secrets outside tracked source files and fail closed when its required production secret is absent.

Before release, a secret scanner reports zero confirmed credentials in tracked files. In production mode, startup without SAIGONBITE_SECRET_KEY fails; with it supplied through deployment configuration, startup does not expose the value in logs. Measurement: scanner report and startup checks; not run in P1.
The system shall serve the public demo over valid HTTPS and redirect public HTTP requests to HTTPS.
Plan D-5; §5.4 HTTPS and secure session cookies

On the demo hostname, the certificate validates, each HTTP request redirects with 301 or 308, and the session cookie has Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite attributes. This deployment target is unmeasured until P6.
The system shall keep key customer, kitchen, shipper, admin, and report pages usable at a 360 CSS-pixel viewport.

At 360 CSS pixels, each key page has document scroll width no greater than viewport width; primary controls are visible and operable without horizontal page scrolling. Measurement: browser viewport inspection at 360 pixels; not run in P1.
The system shall keep presentation, controller, domain, and data-access responsibilities in the layers defined by the plan.

A static import review finds zero SQL or sqlite access in presentation/controllers and zero Flask or SQL imports in the domain layer; database calls occur in data-access modules. Measurement: import scan and architecture review; not run in P1.
The system shall archive closed records without physically deleting them and retain authorized historical access.
Plan §2.4 archive semantics; §3.4 BR-24/Q5; §5.3 archived_at fields; checklist P1-17

After archiving a closed order, its order, line, payment, delivery, and offer row counts are unchanged; operational lists omit it while authorized history, receipt, and report views still include it. Measurement: compare row counts and view results before and after archive; no result recorded in P1.
The system shall serialize competing state changes and preserve order, delivery, and payment consistency when an operation fails.
Case p.2 handoff/responsibility problem; Plan BR-02/BR-11/BR-17/BR-25; §3.3; §5.2; §7.2

Planned P4 method: synchronize contenders with a barrier and use independent database connections for last kitchen slot, one READY pickup, accept versus cancel, and cancel versus start preparing. Exclusive claims have one durable winner and a controlled loser message. Other races allow a legal serialized outcome, including accept then cancel; a stale answer never revives a closed order. Force insert and COMMIT failures and require all related writes to roll back. A held write lock yields a controlled retry response without a partial change or HTTP 500. No race or rollback test has run in P1.
